reason: E1 shows that 75% cold rolling and 350 °C/15 min treatment refine grains, precipitate phases, and improve strength and corrosion in a Ti–Nb–Mo–Sn alloy, but none of the cited evidence demonstrates these effects in a high-entropy alloy; E2–E4 only provide general context about HEA properties or processing without supporting the specific thermo-mechanical response claimed.
premises: 75% cold rolling refines grain size in the target HEA
Heating at 350 °C for 15 min after cold rolling precipitates secondary phases
Grain refinement and precipitates increase strength and reduce creep
Grain refinement and precipitates improve corrosion resistance
The cited Ti-alloy results generalize to high-entropy alloys for aerospace fasteners
